notes:
WHAT WAS CHECKED: Mem0's LoCoMo claims (arxiv 2504.19413) against the paper's own results table, Zep's public rebuttal, Mem0's GitHub challenge to Zep, Mem0's current marketing pages, Letta's counter-experiment, and an independent audit of the LoCoMo benchmark itself. All URLs listed were actually fetched.

(1) PAPER'S OWN NUMBERS — CONFIRMED AS SELF-REPORTED, AND YES, FULL-CONTEXT IS HIGHER THAN MEM0. From the paper's results table (arxiv.org/html/2504.19413v1): Mem0 J=66.88±0.15, Mem0-graph J=68.44±0.17, OpenAI memory J=52.90±0.14, Full-context J=72.90±0.19, Zep (as Mem0 configured it)=65.99±0.16, LangMem=58.10, A-Mem=48.38. So the full-context baseline beats Mem0's best variant by ~4.5 points in Mem0's own paper — Mem0 is not SOTA on answer quality even by its own measurement; its claim is an efficiency tradeoff (reported p95 latency 1.44s vs 17.12s, >90% token savings). The '26% relative improvement over OpenAI' is arithmetically correct (66.88/52.90=1.264) but is measured against Mem0's own implementation and run of the OpenAI memory baseline — not independently verified. The ~90% token-savings figure is likewise a vendor self-measurement with no third-party verification; a separate independent audit of a different vendor (EverMemOS) found claimed token reductions overstated (67% real vs 89% claimed), illustrating that such claims routinely fail scrutiny, though that specific finding is not about Mem0.

(2) ZEP DISPUTE — UNRESOLVED, BOTH SIDES' NUMBERS CONTESTED. Timeline: Mem0's CTO (Deshraj) opened getzep/zep-papers issue #5 (May 8, 2025) alleging Zep's 84% headline improperly included the adversarial category-5 questions and claiming a corrected Zep score of 58.44±0.20; the paper prints Zep at 65.99. Zep's rebuttal blog ('Is Mem0 Really SOTA in Agent Memory?') alleges three configuration errors in Mem0's evaluation of Zep: (a) both conversation participants assigned the 'user' role in a graph model designed for user-assistant pairs, (b) timestamps appended to message text instead of Zep's created_at field, breaking temporal reasoning, (c) sequential instead of parallel searches inflating Zep's reported latency. Zep claims its corrected self-score is 75.14±0.17 (~10% relative above Mem0's best) and pointedly notes Mem0's own full-context baseline (~73%) beats Mem0 (~68%). NO public Mem0 response to Zep's three specific configuration allegations was found — not in the issue thread, not on Mem0's research/blog pages. Neither side's number is independently reproducible because the contested configuration choices (API version, category inclusion, timestamp handling) are not prescribed by the benchmark.

(3) INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTIONS — NONE CONFIRM MEM0'S NUMBERS; ADJACENT EVIDENCE IS UNFLATTERING. (a) Letta (a competitor, so an interested party, but independent of both disputants) reported 74.0% on LoCoMo using GPT-4o-mini with a plain filesystem plus grep/search tools — no memory system at all — beating Mem0's best 68.5% graph variant; Letta also states Mem0 did not respond to requests for implementation details of its benchmarking. (b) The dial481/locomo-audit repo (Penfield Labs) audited the benchmark itself: 99 of 1,540 questions (6.4%) have wrong golden answers (honest ceiling ~93.6%), the LLM judge accepted ~63% of intentionally wrong vague-but-topical answers, and category sample sizes are so unequal that many per-category system comparisons are statistically indistinguishable from noise. It does not reproduce Mem0's specific scores. (c) No true third-party reproduction of Mem0's 66.88 figure was found anywhere.

ADDITIONAL RED FLAG: Mem0's current research page (mem0.ai/research) now claims 92.5 overall on LoCoMo (single-hop 94.6, multi-hop 95.4, temporal 82.3; mean tokens 6,956), attributed on their blog to an April 2026 algorithm update, with no published reconciliation of the jump from 66.9 and no mention of Zep's criticisms. Given the audit's finding that LoCoMo's honest ceiling is ~93.6% and its judge is highly lenient, scores in the 92-95 range (Zep reportedly claims 94.7 via secondary sources) are at or near the corrupted ceiling and should not be treated as meaningful differentiation.

BOTTOM LINE: The headline numbers (66-68% J, 26% over OpenAI, ~90% token savings) accurately quote the paper, but the paper itself shows full-context winning on quality; the cross-vendor comparisons are contested with credible specific misconfiguration allegations that Mem0 has not publicly answered; no independent party has reproduced Mem0's scores; and the benchmark itself has documented ground-truth and judge defects that undermine fine-grained claims by every vendor.
corrected_numbers: Per Mem0's own paper (2504.19413) results table: Mem0 J=66.88±0.15; Mem0-graph J=68.44±0.17; OpenAI memory J=52.90±0.14; Full-context J=72.90±0.19 (HIGHER than Mem0 by ~4.5-6 points); Zep-as-measured-by-Mem0 J=65.99±0.16 (Zep's own corrected claim: 75.14±0.17). '26% relative over OpenAI' = 66.88/52.90, valid arithmetic against Mem0's own baseline run only. Letta independent counter-result: 74.0% on LoCoMo with filesystem+grep, no memory system. Mem0's current marketing claim of 92.5 (April 2026 algorithm) is unreconciled with the paper and unverified; LoCoMo's audited honest ceiling is ~93.6% with a judge that accepts ~63% of intentionally wrong answers.

notes:
WHAT WAS CHECKED: Zep's paper (arXiv 2501.13956, full text via ar5iv), Zep's two blog posts, the MemGPT paper listing, the official LongMemEval repo, the Mem0-filed GitHub dispute issue, Emergence and Mastra benchmark pages, an academic paper on benchmark-design sensitivity, and HN for community discussion.

(1) DMR CLAIM — NUMBERS ACCURATE, SIGNIFICANCE NOT. The 94.8% (Zep, gpt-4-turbo) vs 93.4% (MemGPT) figures are correctly quoted from Zep's paper. But DMR is a small synthetic benchmark: 500 conversations from the Multi-Session Chat dataset, 5 sessions of up to 12 messages each (~60 messages total), one LLM-judged QA pair per conversation, introduced by the MemGPT team. Three problems: (a) apples-to-oranges — the 93.4% is cited from MemGPT's paper, not re-run; Zep's paper admits they were 'unable to reproduce MemGPT's results using gpt-4o-mini due to insufficient methodological details'; (b) saturation — Zep's own paper reports that a no-memory-system full-context baseline scores 94.4% (gpt-4-turbo) and 98.0% (gpt-4o-mini), so Zep's marginal value over context-stuffing on DMR is 0.4pp / 0.2pp (~2 of 500 questions); (c) noise — a 1.4pp gap on n=500 at ~94% is within one binomial standard error (~1.1pp); no significance test reported. To Zep's credit, the paper itself calls DMR inadequate (single-turn fact retrieval, ambiguous phrasing, poor enterprise representativeness); the 'new SOTA' marketing framing survives anyway.

(2) LONGMEMEVAL — CLAIMS ACCURATELY REPORTED, NOT INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED. Paper reports, on LongMemEval_S (~115k-token histories, 500 questions, ICLR 2025 benchmark by Wu et al.): gpt-4o 60.2%→71.2%, gpt-4o-mini 55.4%→63.8%; latency 28.9s→2.58s and 31.3s→3.20s. Caveats: the '18.5% improvement' is relative (+11.0pp absolute); the '90% latency reduction' is vs the slowest possible baseline (entire 115k-token history stuffed in-prompt) — any retrieval system achieves a similar win, and reported latency excludes graph-ingestion cost. I found NO independent reproduction: the LongMemEval authors' official repo has no leaderboard including Zep; Mastra's leaderboard cites Zep's 71.2% from Zep's own paper rather than re-running; Emergence compares against 71.2% without stating a re-run. Several 2026 listicles assert the number was 'independently reproduced' but cite no harness or source — they echo the identical 71.2%, indicating citation, not replication. Treat as vendor-reported. Context: later self-reported results (all also unverified, different judge/actor models) place 71.2% mid-table — Emergence 86% with plain RAG (their conclusion: 'advanced memory architecture appears to be overkill for LongMemEval'), Supermemory 81.6–85.2%, Hindsight 83.6–91.4%, Mastra 94.87%.

(3) DISPUTES. The Mem0-Zep benchmark war (over LoCoMo, not DMR/LongMemEval, but bearing on methodology trust): Mem0's paper evaluated Zep unfavorably; Zep's rebuttal blog ('Lies, Damn Lies, & Statistics') alleges Mem0 misconfigured Zep (both speakers given user role, timestamps appended to text instead of the created_at field, sequential instead of parallel searches) and claims a corrected 75.14%±0.17; Mem0's CTO Deshraj filed getzep/zep-papers issue #5 (May 8, 2025) alleging Zep's own 84% LoCoMo claim corrects to 58.44%±0.20 due to a category-inclusion error (adversarial Category 5 in numerator but not denominator), non-standard system_prompt/retrieval template vs other baselines, and single-run reporting vs 10-run averages. No response from Zep in that thread and no neutral third-party adjudication of either side. An academic paper (arXiv 2605.24060) independently shows memory-system rankings can 'silently flip' with single benchmark-design choices, which is consistent with this dispute pattern. HN discussion of Zep's paper was negligible (1 point, 0 comments).

BOTTOM LINE: Substantiated — Zep's numbers exist as stated in their arXiv paper (not peer-reviewed; ICLR-benchmark refers to LongMemEval itself, not Zep's paper) and the DMR/LongMemEval figures are internally consistent. Marketing — 'beats MemGPT' (different harness, within noise, benchmark saturated per Zep's own baselines), 'SOTA' (superseded on LongMemEval by multiple self-reported systems including plain RAG), and the 90% latency framing (vs deliberately slow full-context baseline, ingestion cost excluded). The LongMemEval result is plausible and directionally reasonable but remains vendor-reported with no independent replication found as of Aug 2026.
corrected_numbers: DMR: Zep 94.8% (gpt-4-turbo) / 98.2% (gpt-4o-mini) vs Zep's own full-context (no memory system) baselines of 94.4% / 98.0% — true memory-system delta ~0.4pp (~2 of 500 questions); MemGPT 93.4% cited from MemGPT paper, never re-run by Zep. LongMemEval_S: Zep 71.2% (gpt-4o) / 63.8% (gpt-4o-mini) vs full-context 60.2% / 55.4% — '18.5%' is relative improvement (+11.0pp absolute); latency 2.58s vs 28.9s (gpt-4o). Disputed LoCoMo figures (separate benchmark): Zep claimed 84%, Mem0's re-run says 58.44%±0.20, Zep's counter-corrected claim is 75.14%±0.17 — unresolved.
